subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Prove that the point of intersection of two perpendicular tangents to the hyperbola x²/a² − y²/b² − 1 = 0 lies on the circle x² + y² = a² − b².

mark_split.label: Set up the tangent through P

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Senior Inter Maths-2B (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.67 — SAQ chapter 9 Hyperbola, answer 80, and repeated verbatim as the third sub-item of the Bullet Model Paper's Q15 (book p.109). NOT on an SSP page (book p.49's 13-page SSP list includes p.66 but not p.67). Printed appearance: TS 16,17. Book p.67 prints no margin mark tags for this proof-style question, so the 1+1+1+1 split here is OURS, following the four natural stages of the standard 'product of roots' proof — the same split pattern used on the analogous Ellipse director-circle card (book p.63, answer 72), with a²+b² replaced by a²−b² throughout since a hyperbola's tangent formula subtracts b² instead of adding it. No error found in the book's printed working. A FIGURE is authored for this card — one branch of the hyperbola, its (smaller, concentric) director circle, and two perpendicular tangent lines from an external point — because the picture IS the argument: seeing the locus point on a circle INSIDE the hyperbola's own vertices (radius √(a²−b²) < a) is the entire content of the result, and it is the opposite size relationship from an ellipse's director circle, which sits OUTSIDE the ellipse. Hyperbola is a SAQ+VSAQ-only unit on the book's IPE Blue Print (book p.5) — 4 marks in Section B (paper slot Q15) and 2 marks in Section A (paper slot Q5); it has NO LAQ chapter and no Section-C slot, so no 7-mark form is authored for this unit. The Bullet Model Paper's Q5 (Hyperbola VSAQ, book p.104) and Q15 (Hyperbola SAQ, book p.109) were diffed against this unit's numbered chapters: all 5 Q5 sub-items reprint answers 130, 131, 132, 137 and 136 verbatim, and all 3 Q15 sub-items reprint answers 78.1, 79.2 and 80 verbatim, so no Bullet Model Paper extra was authored for this unit. No two-book union check and no board back-test were possible for Maths-2B (no second-year TSBIE BLM on hand; the book's five Guess Papers pp.118-127 are the orchestrator's back-test stand-in).

insider_note: Name the result 'director circle' on the final boxed line — examiners often award the last mark for naming it, not just deriving it. Also worth a one-line remark that this circle is real only when a > b.

steps.label: Set up the tangent through P
steps.margin_note: First mark. A tangent with slope m to a hyperbola always has the form y = mx ± √(a²m² − b²).
steps.memory_tip: Start every 'tangents through a point' hyperbola proof the same way: write the tangent-with-slope-m formula, then force it through the given point.
lines: Let the hyperbola be S ≡ x²/a² − y²/b² − 1
Let P(x₁, y₁) be a point on the locus.
Tangent with slope m: y = mx ± √(a²m² − b²)
If it passes through P(x₁, y₁):
steps.why: Forcing the general hyperbola tangent to pass through the locus point P turns 'a tangent through P' into an algebraic equation relating m to the coordinates of P.
common_mistakes: Using the ellipse tangent formula (+b² under the root) instead of the hyperbola one (−b²).
Substituting P into the hyperbola equation itself instead of into the tangent line equation.

steps.label: Form the quadratic in m
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Squaring removes the root and produces a quadratic whose two roots are the two tangent slopes.
steps.memory_tip: Two tangents from one point means: look for a QUADRATIC whose two roots are their two slopes.
steps.why: Equation (1) is a quadratic in m; its two roots m₁, m₂ are exactly the slopes of the two tangents that pass through P, since each root satisfies the tangency condition.
common_mistakes: Expanding (y₁ − mx₁)² incorrectly and losing the cross term −2mx₁y₁.
Writing the constant term as (y₁² − b²) instead of (y₁² + b²) — the minus sign in the hyperbola's tangent formula flips again when −b² moves across the equals sign.

steps.label: Apply the perpendicularity condition
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Perpendicular tangents mean the product of the two roots m₁m₂ = −1.
steps.memory_tip: Product of roots of am² + bm + c = 0 is c/a — apply it here with a = (x₁²−a²), c = (y₁²+b²).
lines: If the tangents are perpendicular, m₁m₂ = −1
steps.why: Two lines are perpendicular exactly when the product of their slopes is −1; since m₁ and m₂ are the roots of the quadratic in (1), their product is read off directly from the ratio of its constant and leading coefficients.
common_mistakes: Using sum of roots instead of product of roots — perpendicularity is a PRODUCT condition, not a sum.
Dropping the minus sign when equating the ratio to −1.

steps.label: Conclude the locus
steps.margin_note: Fourth mark. Clear the fraction and simplify — the x₁² and a² terms combine into a circle equation.
steps.memory_tip: The director circle of a hyperbola sits INSIDE the vertices — radius √(a²−b²) is always less than a — the opposite of an ellipse's director circle, which is bigger than the ellipse.
lines: y₁² + b² = −(x₁² − a²) ⇒ x₁² + y₁² = a² − b²

lines.text: Locus of P(x₁, y₁) is x² + y² = a² − b² — the director circle

steps.why: Rearranging the perpendicularity equation shows that every point from which the two tangents are perpendicular satisfies x² + y² = a² − b², which is the equation of a circle concentric with the hyperbola.
common_mistakes: Stopping at y₁² + b² = a² − x₁² without moving all terms to one side to reveal the circle equation.
Not noticing this circle is real only when a > b — if b > a, a² − b² is negative and the locus has no real points, meaning no pair of perpendicular tangents exists at all.

steps.label: The figure
steps.margin_note: No marks — the question does not ask for a diagram. Drawn because the picture IS the argument here.
steps.memory_tip: The director circle is always smaller than the hyperbola's own branches and sits between them, sharing the centre.
steps.why: P sits on the director circle, and the two tangent lines from P touch the (right) branch of the hyperbola at right angles to each other — the whole content of the theorem is visible in this one picture.
common_mistakes: Drawing the director circle bigger than or the same size as the hyperbola's vertex distance — it must be strictly smaller (radius √(a²−b²) < a).
Drawing the two tangent lines from P as if they were parallel rather than perpendicular.
